# SegmentedBar

A segmented bar shows how one whole splits into a few parts (up to 6 by default), as blocks whose widths are
proportional to the amounts. Use it instead of a pie or a donut. To compare the parts with each other or to
show more of them, use a bar chart; for a single ratio against a limit, use Progress.

**Interaction**: hovering a block shows a tooltip with its amount, share and name; the blocks are one `Tab`
stop, and `←` / `→` (`Home` / `End`) move between them, showing the same tooltip. Screen readers read the
label of the bar and then each part as "Name: amount (share)", without hovering. A label that does not fit
in its block is not printed; the value stays in the tooltip and the accessible name. While `loading`, a skeleton
of the same size takes the place of the bar and appears after 200 ms, so fast loads do not flash.

**Category**: Charts · **Common uses**: Storage by file type, time spent per phase, budget split, the split of a figure in a table row

## Import

```ts
import { SegmentedBar } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

A tall bar standing alone: each block prints its share where it fits, and the legend lists the names in block
order. Hover a block, or press `Tab` and then `←` / `→`, to see its amount, share and name.

```tsx
import { Panel, SegmentedBar, Stack, Text } from 'vellum-ui'

const storage = [
  { key: 'images', name: 'Images', value: 413 },
  { key: 'videos', name: 'Videos', value: 286 },
  { key: 'documents', name: 'Documents', value: 92 },
  { key: 'audio', name: 'Audio', value: 41 },
  { key: 'archives', name: 'Archives', value: 18 },
]

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <Text weight="medium">Storage by file type</Text>
        <SegmentedBar
          variant="tall"
          label="Storage by file type"
          items={storage}
          format={(v) => `${v} GB`}
        />
      </Stack>
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Amounts and folding

`show="value"` prints the amount instead of the share. Past `maxItems` parts (6 by default), the tail is folded
into "Other", in the de-emphasis color.

```tsx
import { Panel, SegmentedBar, Stack } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Variants() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <SegmentedBar
          variant="tall"
          label="Budget by team"
          show="value"
          format="compact"
          items={[
            { key: 'engineering', name: 'Engineering', value: 413_000_000 },
            { key: 'design', name: 'Design', value: 182_000_000 },
            { key: 'marketing', name: 'Marketing', value: 96_000_000 },
            { key: 'support', name: 'Support', value: 54_000_000 },
          ]}
        />
        <SegmentedBar
          variant="tall"
          label="Visits by country"
          maxItems={4}
          items={[
            { key: 'us', name: 'United States', value: 4_210 },
            { key: 'de', name: 'Germany', value: 1_830 },
            { key: 'jp', name: 'Japan', value: 1_240 },
            { key: 'br', name: 'Brazil', value: 610 },
            { key: 'in', name: 'India', value: 540 },
            { key: 'fr', name: 'France', value: 320 },
          ]}
        />
      </Stack>
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

### Thin, next to its figures

The thin bar has no text: the figures are beside it. In table rows, use `dense` (4 px) and give the whole table
one legend, here on the bar of the total.

```tsx
import { Box, DataTable, Inline, Panel, SegmentedBar, Stack, Text } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Thin() {
  const tasks = (done: number, review: number, todo: number) => [
    { key: 'done', name: 'Done', value: done },
    { key: 'review', name: 'In review', value: review },
    { key: 'todo', name: 'To do', value: todo },
  ]
  const rows = [
    { name: 'Atlas', done: 24, review: 6, todo: 10 },
    { name: 'Beacon', done: 8, review: 2, todo: 21 },
    { name: 'Cobalt', done: 15, review: 0, todo: 3 },
  ]
  return (
    // The table goes in a flush Panel, so its columns line up with the bar above (padding 5 = the table's inset)
    <Panel flush>
      <Box paddingX={5} paddingY={4}>
        <Stack gap={2}>
          <Inline justify="between">
            <Text weight="medium">All projects</Text>
            <Text size="sm" tone="secondary">
              47 of 89 tasks done
            </Text>
          </Inline>
          <SegmentedBar
            variant="thin"
            legend
            label="Tasks in all projects"
            items={tasks(47, 8, 34)}
          />
        </Stack>
      </Box>
      <DataTable
        aria-label="Projects"
        rowKey={(row) => row.name}
        rows={rows}
        columns={[
          { key: 'name', title: 'Project' },
          {
            key: 'tasks',
            title: 'Tasks',
            width: 240,
            render: (row) => (
              <SegmentedBar
                variant="thin"
                dense
                label={`Tasks in ${row.name}`}
                items={tasks(row.done, row.review, row.todo)}
              />
            ),
          },
        ]}
      />
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## States

### No data

Without parts, or when every part is 0, the bar is an empty track of the same height. Negative or non-finite
values are treated the same way, with a warning in development.

```tsx
import { Panel, SegmentedBar, Stack } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Empty() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Stack gap={4}>
        <SegmentedBar variant="tall" label="Storage by file type" items={[]} />
        <SegmentedBar
          variant="thin"
          label="Tasks"
          items={[
            { key: 'done', name: 'Done', value: 0 },
            { key: 'todo', name: 'To do', value: 0 },
          ]}
        />
      </Stack>
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly SegmentedBarItem[]` | The parts, in the order of the blocks. Each keeps the color of its position (or its `slot`) even when another part is 0 and not drawn. Negative or non-finite values cannot be part of a whole: the bar is then shown empty (with a warning in development). When every value is 0 the bar is empty too. | — | Yes |
| `label` | `string` | What the whole is, such as "Storage by file type". Screen readers read it before the parts. | — | Yes |
| `variant` | `'thin' \| 'tall'` | `tall` (28 px): a bar standing alone, with the share or amount printed in each block that has room for it and a legend. `thin` (8 px): a bar next to the figures it splits (in a table row or above a list), without text or legend. | — | Yes |
| `dense` | `boolean` | Makes the thin bar 4 px high, for dense table rows. | — | No |
| `show` | `'share' \| 'value'` | What the tall blocks print: the `share` of the whole (46%) or the `value` (413M, written with `format`). | `'share'` | No |
| `format` | `ValueFormat` | How amounts are written, in the blocks (with `show="value"`), the tooltip and the accessible names. | `'auto'` | No |
| `maxItems` | `number` | The most parts shown, "Other" included (2–8). Past it, the parts after the first `maxItems - 1` are folded into "Other" in the de-emphasis color, so order the items with the ones to keep first. | `6` | No |
| `legend` | `boolean` | Shows a legend under the bar: the names in block order, without numbers. On by default for `tall`, off for `thin` (in a table, use one legend for the whole table). | — | No |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Shows a skeleton in place of the bar (and of the legend, when there is one) while the data loads; the size does not change when the data arrives. Like Statistic, the skeleton appears after 200 ms, so fast loads do not flash. | — | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### SegmentedBarItem

One part of a SegmentedBar.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Unique key of the part. | — | Yes |
| `name` | `string` | Name of the part, shown in the legend and the tooltip and read by screen readers. | — | Yes |
| `value` | `number` | Amount of the part: a finite number, 0 or more. | — | Yes |
| `slot` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 7 \| 8` | Chart color (1–8). By default the n-th item uses the n-th chart color. | — | No |

### ValueFormat

How a value is written.
- `'auto'`: in full below 10,000, compact from 10,000 on (1,284 · 12.9K · 4.2M).
- `'number'`: always in full, with grouping separators.
- `'compact'`: always compact.
- `'percent'`: the value is a ratio (0.125 → 12.5%).
- a function: your own formatting (units, currencies).

```ts
type ValueFormat = 'auto' | 'number' | 'compact' | 'percent' | ((value: number) => string)
```
